findings.source_passage: What I've dared, I've willed; and what I've willed, I'll do!
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after 'Oh, hard! that to fire others'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most quoted and critically cited lines in the entire chapter, crystallizing Ahab's monomaniacal will as a philosophical and dramatic statement; its absence is a significant signature loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'What I've dared, I've willed; and what I've willed, I'll do!' in the final paragraph.

findings.source_passage: Oh, hard! that to fire others, the match itself must needs be wasting!
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after 'they all stand before me; and I their match'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a rhetorically and interpretively distinctive line — Ahab's self-consuming nature as an agent of destruction — that the critical tradition returns to repeatedly; its loss erases a key layer of self-awareness in Ahab's monologue.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim or near-verbatim: 'Oh, hard! that to fire others, the match itself must needs be wasting!'

findings.source_passage: I laugh and hoot at ye, ye cricket-players, ye pugilists, ye deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes!
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after 'I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer'
findings.why_it_matters: This grotesque, defiant comic catalogue is one of the most stylistically distinctive passages in the chapter, establishing Ahab's taunting of the gods in an unmistakably Melvillean register; replacing it with 'He flung his challenge upward. Come forth!' flattens the voice completely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the taunting address to the gods including 'ye cricket-players, ye pugilists, ye deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes' and the schoolboy bully passage to preserve Ahab's grotesque-comic register.

findings.source_passage: Yonder, by ever-brimming goblet's rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The gold brow plumbs the blue.
findings.why_it_matters: This lyrical sunset imagery is prosodically distinctive and sets up the soul-mounts-up contrast; its absence flattens the poetic texture of the opening meditation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least 'Yonder, by ever-brimming goblet's rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The gold brow plumbs the blue.' before the diver-sun line.

findings.source_passage: my one cogged circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve
findings.why_it_matters: The cogged-circle / wheels metaphor is a critical touchstone for Ahab's mechanical determinism and his manipulation of the crew; it is interpretively significant and stylistically distinctive.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'my one cogged circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve' in the transition to the final paragraph.

findings.source_passage: This lovely light, it lights not me; all loveliness is anguish to me, since I can ne'er enjoy.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft collapses 'This lovely light, it lights not me; all loveliness is anguish to me, since I can ne'er enjoy' to merely 'All loveliness is anguish to me,' losing the anaphoric light/lights construction and the explanatory 'since I can ne'er enjoy' that gives the line its pathos.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'This lovely light, it lights not me; all loveliness is anguish to me, since I can ne'er enjoy.'

summary: The draft preserves the iron-rails peroration and isolated signature phrases but erases three high-priority passages ('What I've dared, I've willed,' the match-wasting line, and the gods-taunting catalogue) along with several medium-weight voice and interpretive passages, producing a significantly flattened Ahab soliloquy.
